title: Théorie de la spéculation
venue: Annales scientifiques de l'École normale supérieure
question: If the market is fair, how must a speculative price move?
changed: Modeled prices as a driftless random walk, built Brownian motion five years before Einstein, and priced options with it.
assumed: Arithmetic Gaussian steps, so a price can go negative.

title: Differential-Space
question: Can a continuous path that moves randomly at every instant be made mathematically rigorous?
changed: Constructed Brownian motion as a probability measure on continuous paths: the Wiener process every later model uses.

title: Stochastic integral
question: How do you integrate against a path that has no derivative anywhere?
changed: Defined the stochastic integral, so dynamics driven by Brownian noise can be written and solved.

title: On a formula concerning stochastic differentials
question: What is the chain rule when the input is a diffusion?
changed: Itô's lemma: a smooth function of a diffusion picks up a second-order term, the source of the −σ²/2 in every log-price drift.

title: Brownian Motion in the Stock Market
question: Which transformation of price behaves like a particle in Brownian motion?
changed: Showed log prices, not prices, diffuse: the log-normal model that fixes negative prices.
assumed: Gaussian log returns with constant variance.

title: The Variation of Certain Speculative Prices
question: Are price changes really Gaussian?
changed: Showed cotton price changes have far fatter tails than a normal law and proposed stable Paretian distributions.
assumed: Infinite variance: stable laws with index below two.

title: Rational Theory of Warrant Pricing
question: How should a long-dated call on a stock be valued?
changed: Put geometric Brownian motion into economics and brought Bachelier back into view, one step short of Black–Scholes.
assumed: An expected return on the warrant chosen by hand, not by hedging.

verified.note: Industrial Management Review (1965) has no registered DOI; only later reprints do.

title: A Subordinated Stochastic Process Model with Finite Variance for Speculative Prices
question: Can fat tails come from something other than infinite variance?
changed: Ran price on a random business clock driven by trading volume: fat tails with finite variance.

title: Martingales and arbitrage in multiperiod securities markets
question: What do all arbitrage-free prices have in common?
changed: Linked no-arbitrage to the existence of an equivalent martingale measure: pricing as expectation under a changed probability.

title: Martingales and stochastic integrals in the theory of continuous trading
question: When can every claim be hedged in continuous time?
changed: Made the martingale approach rigorous in continuous time and tied completeness to martingale representation.

title: The Variance Gamma (V.G.) Model for Share Market Returns
question: Is there a tractable pure-jump process that fits returns' tails?
changed: Brownian motion run on a gamma clock: a Lévy model with skew and kurtosis and a closed-form characteristic function.

title: A general version of the fundamental theorem of asset pricing
question: Exactly which notion of no-arbitrage is equivalent to a martingale measure?
changed: Proved the fundamental theorem in full generality: no free lunch with vanishing risk.

title: Empirical properties of asset returns: stylized facts and statistical issues
question: Which statistical facts must any model of returns reproduce?
changed: Catalogued the stylized facts: heavy tails, volatility clustering, leverage effect, no linear autocorrelation, aggregational Gaussianity.
